'''Michael C. F. Wiescher''' (born 1949 in [[Wuppertal]]) is a German-American experimental nuclear physicist and astrophysicist,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Wiescher, M.|date=August 17, 2009|title=Cosmic alchemy in the laboratory|journal=Physics|volume=2|article-number=69|publisher=American Physical Society|doi=10.1103/Physics.2.69 |bibcode=2009PhyOJ...2...69W |url=https://physics.aps.org/articles/v2/69?referer=rss}}</ref> known for his laboratory research in nuclear physics connected with various astrophysical phenomena such as stellar evolution and explosion environments.<ref name=aps>{{cite web|title=Michael Wiescher|website=American Physical Society (APS)|url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/michael_wiescher}}</ref><ref name=BethePrize>{{cite web|title=2003 Hans A. Bethe Prize Recipient, Michael C. Wiescher|website=American Physical Society|url=https://aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Wiescher&first_nm=Michael%20C&year=2003}}</ref><ref name=ae>{{cite web|title=Michael Wiescher (Membership Number: 4454)|website=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Wiescher_Michael}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Wiescher completed in 1969 his ''[[Abitur]]'' at Gymnasium [[Münchberg]] in [[Bavaria]]. At the [[University of Münster]], he graduated in 1972 with [[Diplom#Germany|''Vordiplom'']] in physics, in 1975 with ''[[Diplom]]'' in solid state physics, and in 1980 with doctorate (''summa cum laude'') in nuclear physics. His doctoral dissertation entitled ''Measurement of the Reactions in the CNO Cycles'' was supervised by [[Claus Rolfs]]. As a post-doc Wiescher was from 1980 to 1983 at the [[Ohio State University]], from 1983 to 1985 under the supervision of [[Karl-Ludwig Kratz]] at the [[University of Mainz]], and from 1985 to 1986 at [[Caltech]]'s Kellogg Radiation Laboratory. At the [[University of Notre Dame]] he was from 1986 to 1990 an assistant professor, from 1990 to 1993, and from 1993 to 1998 a full professor, before his appointment as Freimann Professor of Physics in 1998. In addition to his Freimann Professorship, he was the director of the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Astrophysics]] (JINA) at the University of Notre Dame from 2003-2015<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bardayan Elected Director of ARUNA |url=https://sites.nd.edu/dan-bardayan/news/#:~:text=Nuclear%20Science%20Laboratory%20(NSL)%20Director%20and%20Notre%20Dame%20Professor%20of%20Physics%20Dan%20Bardayan&text=scientific%20impact%20as%20part%20of%20the%20U.S. |website=University of Notre Dame}}</ref> and continued to be director of the [https://isnap.nd.edu/people/ Institute for Structure and Nuclear Astrophysics at Notre Dame]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Department of Physics and Astronomy |url=https://physics.nd.edu/people/faculty/michael-wiescher/ |website=College of Science Department of Physics and Astronomy}}</ref> until 2022, the [[Michigan State University]] and the [[University of Chicago]]. He is also an adjunct professor at Michigan State University and the [[University of Surrey]].<ref name=ae/> He has served as an editorial board member for [[Physical Review|''Physical Review C'']] and as an associate editor for [[Nuclear Physics (journal)|''Nuclear Physics A'']].<ref>{{cite web|title=Candidate Biographies, Nominations for Executive Committee, Michael C. Wiescher|date=November 1999|website=Newsletter No. 120, Division of Nuclear Physics|url=https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/APS/9487474c-539c-4417-81e5-51aeb25847a8/UploadedImages/Documents/120.pdf}}</ref>

He has done research in nuclear astrophysics,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Käppeler, F.|author2=Thielemann, F. K.|author3=Wiescher, M.|year=1998|title=Current quests in nuclear astrophysics and experimental approaches|journal=Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science|volume=48|pages=175–251|doi=10.1146/annurev.nucl.48.1.175 |bibcode=1998ARNPS..48..175K |url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/a210b669cf657cb157957dcfd47c7031/1?pq-origsite=gscholar&cbl=41350|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1088/1742-6596/420/1/012135|title=Experimental Needs and Opportunities in Nuclear Astrophysics |year=2013 |last1=Wiescher |first1=Michael |journal=Journal of Physics: Conference Series |volume=420 |issue=1 |article-number=012135 |bibcode=2013JPhCS.420a2135W |s2cid=123533197 |doi-access=free }} (open access)</ref> low-energy [[experimental physics]], reaction physics with stable and radioactive beams, and analysis of cultural heritage artifacts.<ref name=ae/>

Wiescher is the author or co-author of over 550 research publications.<ref name=ae/> He is the author of local historical writings about his birthplace Wuppertal,<ref>{{cite book|title=Bauern, Weber, Arbeiter – Zur Geschichte der Südhöhen in Barmen|publisher=Verlag H.-J. Momberger|location=Wuppertal|year=2014|isbn=978-3-940439-60-4}} (English translation of title: "Farmers, weavers, workers - On the history of the southern heights in [[Barmen]]")</ref> a biography of [[Arthur E. Haas]],<ref>{{cite book|author=Wiescher, Michael|title=Arthur E. Haas—The Hidden Pioneer of Quantum Mechanics: A Biography|date=23 September 2021 |publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-030-80605-7|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tGpEEAAAQBAJ|postscript=; hbk}}</ref> and the textbook ''Radioaktivität Ursprung und Auswirkungen eines Naturphänomens. Band I'''' (in German),<ref>{{cite book|author=Wiescher, Michael|title=Radioaktivität Ursprung und Auswirkungen eines Naturphänomens. Band I|year=2021|publisher=wbg Academic |isbn=978-3-534-40453-7}} (English translation of title: "Radioactivity. Origin and effects of a natural phenomenon. Volume 1"</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Wiescher publishes book on radioactivity|author=Goethals, Shelly|date=April 9, 2021|website=Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of Notre Dame|url=https://physics.nd.edu/news-events/news/wiescher-publishes-book-on-radioactivity/}}</ref> as well as the co-author, with Khachatur Manukyan, of the textbook ''Scientific Analysis of Cultural Heritage Objects''.<ref>{{cite book|author=Wiescher, Michael|author2=Manukyan, Khachatur|title=Scientific Analysis of Cultural Heritage Objects|date=31 August 2020 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qR78DwAAQBAJ|publisher=Morgan & Claypool|isbn=978-1-68173-916-8|postscript=; pbk}}</ref>

He has given over 200 presentations at national and international conferences.<ref name=aps/> At the 2021 Fall Meeting of the [[American Physical Society|APS]] Division of Nuclear Physics, he presented research, done with Khachatur Manukyan, using X-rays, electron microscopy, and accelerators to investigate coins and paper money from three different historical periods.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nuclear Physicists Track Money Crimes From Ancient Rome to Benjamin Franklin|website=American Physical Society|date=September 9, 2021|url=https://www.aps.org/newsroom/vpr/dnp/2021/20-09-2021-3.cfm}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Wiescher, Michael C.|author2=Manukyan, Khachatur|title=It's all about the Money|journal=APS Division of Nuclear Physics Meeting Abstracts|volume=2021|page=BA-001|year=2021|bibcode=2021APS..DNP.BA001W |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021APS..DNP.BA001W/abstract}}</ref>

Wiescher was elected in 1998 a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS),<ref name=APS>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1998&unit_id=&institution=University+of+Notre+Dame}} (search on year=1998 and institution=University of Notre Dame)</ref> in 2009 a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Elected Fellows, Listing of Fellows who are current members|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing}} (search on last name: Wiescher)</ref> and in 2017 a foreign member of [[Academia Europaea]].<ref name=ae/> He received in 2003 the [[Hans A. Bethe Prize]] of the APS,<ref name=BethePrize/> in 2007 the [[Humboldt Prize]] of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]],<ref>{{cite web|author=Gilroy, William G.|author2=Falda, Wayne|date=June 3, 2007|title=Wiescher selected to receive Humboldt fellowship|website=Notre Dame News, University of Notre Dame|url=https://news.nd.edu/news/wiescher-selected-to-receive-humboldt-fellowship/}}</ref> and in 2018 the LAD Laboratory Astrophysics Prize of the [[American Astronomical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 LAD Laboratory Astrophysics Prize Goes to Michael Wiescher|website=Laboratory Astrophysics Division (LAD), American Astronomical Society (AAS)|date=28 December 2017 |url=https://lad.aas.org/prizes/2018_lab_astro_prize}}</ref> Wiescher was the visiting Heraeus Professor in Frankfurt in 2018-2020 and a Wolfson [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] at the [[University of Edinburgh]] from 2021 to 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Wiescher |url=https://physics.nd.edu/people/michael-wiescher/ |website=University of Notre Dame}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Wiescher Receives British Royal Society Wolfson Fellowship |url=https://www.jinaweb.org/news/michael-wiescher-receives-british-royal-society-wolfson-fellowship |website=Jina-Cee}}</ref>

His doctoral students include [[Hendrik Schatz]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Michael C. Wiescher|website=Physics Tree|url=https://academictree.org/physics/tree.php?pid=203648&fontsize=1&pnodecount=4&cnodecount=2}}</ref>
